summary: Djerba Zarzis International Airport (DJE) is the main gateway to the island of Djerba, one of Tunisia's premier beach and resort destinations. Located in the town of Mellita, the airport handles a large volume of seasonal charter traffic from Europe, serving the island's thriving tourism industry. It is one of the country's busiest airports during peak summer months.
faqs:
Q: How far is Djerba Zarzis International Airport from the main resort areas?
A: The airport is centrally located on Djerba island, with most major hotels and resorts within a 15-30 minute drive.

Q: Does the airport have international flight connections?
A: Yes, it receives flights from many European cities, particularly France, Germany, and the UK, as well as some North African and Middle Eastern destinations.

Q: Are there currency exchange facilities at the airport?
A: Yes, currency exchange services and ATMs are available in the terminal building.

Q: What is the typical flight season for Djerba?
A: The airport operates year-round but sees peak traffic between April and October, when most European charter flights operate.
transport_tips: Taxis are readily available outside the terminal and offer fixed or metered rates to destinations across the island; agree on a fare before departure. Renting a car is straightforward and recommended for those wanting to explore the island independently. Shared shuttle services and hotel transfers are commonly pre-arranged by tour operators.
local_tip: Visit the nearby Djerba Explore complex or take a short drive to Houmt Souk's old medina for authentic local crafts and spices—the airport's compact size means you can check in for your return flight and still have time for a last shopping stop on the island.
